title: A wider turn at the same speed
hook: Change turn radius and predict centripetal acceleration.
misconception: centripetal acceleration doubles when turn radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply a_c = v²/r to compare centripetal acceleration when turn radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With uniform circular motion with fixed speed, a_c = v²/r. When turn radius doubles, centripetal acceleration becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model a_c = v²/r; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider uniform circular motion with fixed speed, with a nonzero initial result. If turn radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on centripetal acceleration?
recall.why: Apply a_c = v²/r under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
